messages:
olivia: FYI hitting a weird onboarding issue — sample-app keeps using org key instead of project key, requests show up on the wrong billing org :confused:

sam: can you paste what env vars are set in CI vs local? names matter here (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY)

olivia: local .env has `REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_abc123`, CI has `REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY=org_xyz789`. SDK logs show: "Using credential from ENV: REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY" — surprised since we expected project-local key to win

mira: SDK resolution order has been a bit unintuitive historically. quick reminder: it should be obvious which key is used when onboarding, we should avoid silent cross-org billing

sam: current (legacy) order is: 1) CLI --key, 2) REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY, 3) REDWOOD_API_KEY, 4) config file. We assumed org-level keys were rarer but that bites when CI injects an org key into all jobs

alex: why was org key above project key in the first place? was that an intentional design decision for back compat? :thinking_face:

sam: historical reasons (org ops flows). But we shouldn't surprise new users. Proposal: change priority to prefer project-scoped env (`REDWOOD_API_KEY`) over org env, and only use org env when project key missing

mira: +1. Also suggest emitting a dev-mode warning when both vars exist and differ, something like: "Ambiguous credentials detected — using REDWOOD_API_KEY from project .env. If you intended to use REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY, set --use-org-key or update CI."

olivia: also need a docs snippet and a migration helper. sample-app README should recommend `REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY` as explicit opt-in to avoid collisions with organization-wide keys in CI

sam: OK. I'll add a small resolution table to the SDK README and a one-line indicator when running in interactive/dev mode. Also plan to emit minimal telemetry event `credential_resolution` with `source` so we can measure freq of collisions (no secrets sent)

cred-lint-bot: cred-lint found 1 ambiguous-key occurrence in repo `sample-app` (path: .github/workflows/ci.yml) — https://ci.internal/cred-lint/12345 :robot_face:

mira: nice, that CI link helps. We should add a lint rule that flags both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY present in the same environment

sam: will add lint rule + tests. Also adding rotation test: if org key rotates and project key still present, SDK must keep using project key and surface auth errors tied to the right key (so retry/rotation flows don't escalate)

alex: timeline? can we get the change + docs in next sprint? :calendar:

sam: I'll open PR today, mark it as low-risk behavioral change, include migration notes and changelog entry. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/333 

olivia: awesome — I'll update sample-app, onboarding checklist, and add a short snippet in the quickstart: 
```
# recommended .env for project-local keys
REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_...
# avoid setting REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY in project CI unless intentionally using org-scoped flows
```

mira: thanks — after PR lands, ops can flip any CI org-wide envs that are accidental. we'll also add doc blurb about rotation: prefer short-lived project keys and rotate org keys with care

olivia: thanks team! this should reduce a bunch of onboarding support tickets :party_parrot:
